why: You cut the array into contiguous blocks of length at most threshold and pay each block's maximum: a partition DP where best[i] = min over the last block length j <= threshold of best[i - j] + max(arr[i-j..i-1]).
hints: Think about the last block of an optimal partition of the first i elements: it has some length j between 1 and threshold.
best[i] = min over j of best[i - j] + max of the last j elements; growing j one step at a time lets you update that maximum in O(1).
Fill best[0..n] with best[0] = 0, two nested loops: O(n * threshold) time, O(n) space.
pitfalls: Blocks may have different lengths; fixed-size chunks of length threshold are not always optimal.
Do not let j exceed i (the block cannot start before index 0).
Compute the block maximum incrementally, otherwise the solution becomes O(n * threshold^2).
constraints: • Not stated in the source (the screenshot shows none). Reasonable bounds: 1 <= arr.length <= 10^4, 1 <= threshold <= arr.length, 0 <= arr[i] <= 10^9; an O(n * threshold) solution is expected.
